Doctor routes declare mutating for all 35 bridges: 15 read-only, 2 add-only, 18 mutates

label: Frontmatter tool grants cannot discriminate risk: all 45 commands declare Bash, 33 also declare Write or Edit, and the 12 declaring neither still mutate through shell calls such as /doctor:install, /doctor:update, /doctor:symlink and /doctor:overlay.

25 of 45 commands already accept an [:auto|:confirm] execution-mode suffix in their own argument-hint, and the 20 without it are exactly the 17 doctor commands plus /speckit:handoff, /speckit:save and /speckit:search.

doctor/_routes.yaml is the only machine-readable risk declaration in the tree: 33 route blocks plus 2 mcp_subroutes carry mutating read-only, add-only or mutates, and most also carry gate3_location naming the concrete write target; the tally is 15 read-only, 2 add-only, 18 mutates.

The 15 read-only routes are exactly the 15 entries with readOnly true in the TypeScript projection, verifying the deriver mapping mutating===read-only to readOnly:true end to end: the risk signal reaches the scorer and stops before the JSON inventory and the output contract.

No non-doctor source declares risk: mutating appears in none of the three command-metadata.json files and allow-list.json carries only a free-text reason, so the readOnly path is starved for the other 28 commands because the data was never authored.

Name-based risk judgement fails in both directions: /doctor:install has only a guide:read-only route while /doctor:env has a mutates route, so install sounds dangerous and env sounds harmless while the manifest says the reverse.

A three-tier reversibility ladder already governs the repository, with trivially reversible work proceeding, reversible-with-effort stating its undo cost, and irreversible work requiring a written rollback plus an explicit yes, and an install still waiting for a yes.

Applying the ladder to declared data: 17 doctor bridges are safe to start unasked (15 read-only plus 2 add-only to scratch), 18 need a question (mutates), and the other 28 commands have no declared answer, with /design:extract and the /deep:* family the only clear out-of-repo or budget-spending cases.

direction: A risk classifier built on allowed-tools or command names
reason: Bash is universal across all 45 commands and names invert the manifest truth on /doctor:install and /doctor:env
